name: compare-grams
description:
How the grams of my text differ from the competitors' texts: a row per gram met in any competitor.

The density of a gram in a text is its count / the words of that text; a competitor without the gram counts as 0. Grams are those of ngrams. With lemmas, a word without a lemma (a single letter, an abbreviation or a unit: «г», «руб», «см») is in no gram, but counts in the words of a text.
n: how many words in a gram.
lemmas: compare lemmas of the words («диваны» is «диван»).
stopwords: on, every word makes grams; off (the default), only the words that are no stopwords.
tolerance: how far from the norm a density is still within, a share of the norm (0.3 is ±30 %).
norm: «median» (the default) or «mean»: the density the verdict and the recommended occurrences go by.
words: the size of the text to recommend occurrences for, in words; by default the words of my text.
per_text: add a density column per competitor text, named by its url column when the table of the competitors has one, else text_1, text_2…
no_digits: leave out the words with a digit of every count, the words total included, as text-stats does.
exclude: words to leave out of every count the same way, as written, with case and ё folded, not by lemma.

The columns: ngram; docs, the competitors that hold it; docs_share, docs / competitors, 0..1; median, mean, min, max, the density in the competitors; mine, its density in my text; verdict, «below», «within» or «above», mine against norm x (1 ± tolerance), and when the norm is 0, «within» if mine is 0, else «above»; need, the norm x `words`, rounded to a whole number of occurrences; have, the occurrences in my text; add, need - have (negative: remove); med_count, the median number of occurrences in the competitors. Densities are rounded to 4 decimals. Sorted by median, biggest first, then ngram. With per_text, the density columns come last.

competitors: a file with the texts of the competitors, one per row, in its first text column; the file is read like `read` does. A url column, if the file has one, names the columns of --per-text.

The step takes the working column as my text (its cells, one per line); the table of the comparison replaces the current one.

Example: semkit read --whole mine.txt compare-grams --competitors competitors.csv write out.csv

options.description: how many words in a gram.

options.description: compare lemmas of the words («диваны» is «диван»).

options.description: on, every word makes grams; off (the default), only the words that are no stopwords.

options.name: --tolerance
options.description: how far from the norm a density is still within, a share of the norm (0.3 is ±30 %).

options.name: --norm
options.description: «median» (the default) or «mean»: the density the verdict and the recommended occurrences go by.

options.name: --words
options.description: the size of the text to recommend occurrences for, in words; by default the words of my text.

options.name: --per-text
options.description: add a density column per competitor text, named by its url column when the table of the competitors has one, else text_1, text_2…

options.description: words to leave out of every count the same way, as written, with case and ё folded, not by lemma. Items: a comma list 'a,b', @FILE (one item per line, or the first column of a table) or @NAME of a list.

arguments.description: a file with the texts of the competitors, one per row, in its first text column; the file is read like `read` does. A url column, if the file has one, names the columns of --per-text. The same as --competitors COMPETITORS.
